survey.q1_answer: keep all (the 8 usage-log flows), leading with Employment Rights Bill, MM: Tech Expo 2026, Tech Expo 2026, Case Study: Paul Tanner
survey.q4_shared_outbound: NO — and the reason is the finding: "No - they read like AI slop tbh". First outright rejection of the company layer, on copy quality, from the team's most prolific flow builder.
survey.chooser: "Vertical then persona and leading with a module if we have an idea of their pain" — a THIRD routing dimension (Nory module) that the agent's model does not carry; also "or target certain events".
survey.wants_new_flows_note: "It would be handy to automate the addition of real world triggers or specifics about the individual I'm targeting. But I hate the idea of sending emails that are clearly using AI syntax." That is the agent's signal layer described precisely, with a hard quality bar attached. For this rep the anti-AI gate is not a nicety, it is the whole deal.
survey.book_note: THE ENTERPRISE REP, and the inverse of every other book: 212 accounts, 97 ICP-fit, but 80 ENT / 15 MM / 2 SMB. 2,575 contacts across 97 accounts (~26 each — deep buying committees, vs ~5 on the BDR books). Personas Ops 473, Finance 199, C-Suite 167, Founder 166: Ops-led with Finance second, where the SMB books run Founder second. 17 reactivation.
survey.accounts_note: Offered unprompted, like William's 15. SIX of the eight are franchise groups — a segment the vertical model does not carry at all.

findings.per_rep_model_vindicated: Magnus and William are the two poles and no single matrix could serve both. William: SMB BDR, 717 ICP, ONE flow plus hand-tailored openers. Magnus: ENT AE, 97 ICP, 34 flows routed by vertical x persona x module. The UKI decision to look flows up per rep rather than build them from a shared pattern is now evidenced from both ends.
findings.company_layer_quality: First rep to reject the shared Outbound layer outright, and it was on copy quality: "they read like AI slop". Lars runs it happily and Louis Gilbert partly; Magnus, who builds the most flows himself, will not touch it. Worth a look at that copy before more reps are pointed at it.
findings.third_routing_dimension_module: He routes on Nory MODULE as well as vertical and persona — his flows carry it in their names (Coffee: Labour, QSR: Labour, AE FLOW - Labour Assessment/AgenticAI Schedules), and his own account list annotates one as 'inventory focused'. The agent models suite (IM vs Full Suite) but not module. Gap.
findings.open_question_4_pubs_bars: More evidence: four of his flows are pub-specific and already tagged pubs_bars (Pubs 25-50 sites x Finance/Ops/IT, Louis > Pubs 25-50 sites).
findings.open_question_10_it_persona: Direct evidence: he runs 'Pubs 25-50 sites: IT Persona' and two IT-tagged Tech Expo flows. IT is a real persona for the ENT motion, not a theoretical gap. His unmapped contact titles also surface 'head of people' — the People persona.
findings.franchise_segment: Six of his eight target accounts are franchise operators (Yum! brands, GDK, three Costa franchises, BWG/Bagel Factory), and he has a 'Domino's Franchise Owners' flow from April. Franchisee groups are a distinct ENT motion with none of the four verticals describing them.
findings.era_angle_cross_validated: His most recently edited flow is 'Employment Rights Bill' (9 Sep) — the same Employment Rights Act angle just built into William's V4 Email 4 off the conjunctural register. Two reps reaching for it independently.

name_collision: 'Tech Expo 2026' exists twice — his own (Events folder) and Josh Savill's shared one. Both are marked live:true by the 'keep all'; if the matcher ever has to choose, ask him which.
matcher_observation: Verified 2026-09-18: his own confirmed flows win for every cell tried, correctly — pubs_bars x ops/finance/IT all resolve to his 'Pubs 25-50 sites' set as 'confirmed'. One tie-break to watch: coffee_cafe + operations resolves to 'Ops Managers' (persona-tagged, no vertical, and it lives in his Domino's folder) rather than 'Coffee: Labour' (vertical-tagged, no persona) — the specificity score treats a persona hit as tighter than a vertical hit. Not wrong, both are his, but if he says Coffee: Labour is a workhorse then the tie-break needs revisiting. Survey #2 Q3 asks which flows carry his volume, which will settle it.
